question: An 80-year-old man is admitted with a sudden picture of aphasia and right hemiparesis. As background highlights, hypertension, well controlled diet and cognitive impairment in the last year under study by his neurologist. Emergency cranial CT demonstrates a left frontal lobar hematoma without contrast enhancement. What is the most likely cause of the hematoma?

options.opa: Arteriovenous malformation masked by the acute hematoma.
options.opc: Vasculitis isolated from the nervous system.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "80-year-old man" -> "sudden aphasia and right hemiparesis" -> "left frontal lobar hematoma" -> "amyloid deposition in cerebral vessels" -> "amyloid cerebral angiopathy" -> 85%

CHAIN: "80-year-old man" -> "sudden aphasia and right hemiparesis" -> "left frontal lobar hematoma" -> "chronic hypertension" -> "small vessel disease" -> "possible chronic arterial hypertension" -> 70%
CHAIN: "80-year-old man" -> "sudden aphasia and right hemiparesis" -> "left frontal lobar hematoma" -> "vascular abnormality" -> "possible arteriovenous malformation" -> 60%
CHAIN: "80-year-old man" -> "sudden aphasia and right hemiparesis" -> "left frontal lobar hematoma" -> "cognitive impairment" -> "amyloid deposition" -> "amyloid cerebral angiopathy" -> 80%
CHAIN: "80-year-old man" -> "sudden aphasia and right hemiparesis" -> "left frontal lobar hematoma" -> "no contrast enhancement" -> "unlikely brain tumor" -> 50%
CHAIN: "80-year-old man" -> "sudden aphasia and right hemiparesis" -> "left frontal lobar hematoma" -> "inflammation of blood vessels" -> "possible vasculitis" -> 40%
analysis: The patient is an elderly man with a sudden onset of neurological symptoms and a lobar hematoma. Given his age and the location of the hematoma, amyloid cerebral angiopathy is the most likely cause. This condition is common in older adults and is characterized by the deposition of amyloid in the walls of cerebral blood vessels, leading to lobar hemorrhages. The absence of contrast enhancement on CT makes a brain tumor less likely, and the sudden presentation is not typical for vasculitis. Chronic hypertension usually causes deep brain hemorrhages rather than lobar ones.
